1	# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)
2	
3	Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
4	Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
5	MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.
6	
7	The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
8	`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
9	fake unless asked.
10	
11	This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.
12	
13	## What success looks like
14	
15	- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
16	- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
17	- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
18	- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
19	  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.
20	
21	If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
22	fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.
23	
24	## Turn it on
25	
26	Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.
27	
28	`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:
29	
30	```json
31	"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
32	```
33	
34	JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
35	the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.
36	
37	Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
38	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
39	`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
40	either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
41	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
42	`orca`.
43	
44	**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
45	as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
46	Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
47	`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
48	`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
49	`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.
50	
51	Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
52	config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
53	is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.
54	
55	The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
56	**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.
57	
58	## Drive state
59	
60	Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
61	fake rereads it about once a second.
62	
63	```json
64	{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
65	```
66	
67	| Field | Meaning |
68	|---|---|
69	| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
70	| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
71	| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
72	| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
73	
74	Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.
75	
76	## Print
77	
78	Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
79	The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.
80	
81	If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
82	menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
83	scenario after send.
84	
85	## Isolate a running app (agents)
86	
87	Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.
88	
89	On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
90	a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
91	`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
92	`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.
93	
94	Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
95	posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
96	half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
97	title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
98	for Print.
99	
100	Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
101	use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.
102	
103	## Unit tests
104	
105	`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
106	control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
107	test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.
108	
109	## Agent id
110	
111	Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
112	id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

content.text:
The last two commits build a printer-management feature for JusPrin's Home screen, and I couldn't find anything broken in them.

**What the commits do:**
- [c11c8d3cb1](https://github.com) makes "Add a printer" actually create a visible printer. Before this, OrcaSlicer had no concept of a "printer" object — adding one only installed a preset behind the scenes, so Home never showed a card for it. Now it saves a named user profile and Home lists it with a menu (Printer settings, Rename, Remove printer).
- [33c2eddd75](https://github.com) fixes the other way to add a printer: Orca's own "set it up myself" wizard bypassed all of that, so a printer added that way silently never appeared on Home. Now the wizard's result gets named too.

**How I tested it:** I couldn't get visual/click access — you declined the screen-control permission prompt for OrcaSlicer — so I ran the project's own automated test paths instead of guessing from a screenshot:

1. Rebuilt the app (binary was current, matched the latest commit).
2. Ran the unit test suite (`jusprin_tests`): **319 assertions across 55 test cases, all pass.**
3. Ran the project's shell integration harness in `--printer-setup` mode, which actually launches the real app in-process and drives the exact flows these commits touch — opening the printer-setup dialog, adding a printer, renaming it, removing it, switching nozzles, and running Orca's own wizard through `run_manual_setup`. **150 checks, all pass, 0 failures**, including the specific ones for these two commits: `named_home_lists_both_printers_by_name`, `named_home_offers_the_printer_menu`, `named_rename_of_the_selected_printer`, `named_remove_of_the_selected_printer_selects_its_parent`, `named_wizard_install_becomes_a_printer`, `named_wizard_names_only_new_models`, and others.

So on this branch, at least the printer-add/rename/remove/wizard-naming flow works correctly — I found no evidence supporting "most features are broken." # JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

content.text:
Both bugs are fixed with four small, targeted changes, verified by real clicks in the running app plus the full automated test suite (319 unit assertions + 150 harness checks, all passing). Here's what changed and why, in plain terms:

**Bug 1 — Home's printer list didn't update after "set it up myself" until you restarted the app.**

The root cause was a race, not a rendering glitch. When you click "+ Add printer" → "set it up myself," the flow is: the dialog closes immediately (`EndModal`), and the actual work — opening Orca's wizard, letting you pick a printer, naming it — happens afterward via a deferred callback (`CallAfter`). But the code that pushes the updated printer list to the Home screen only ran once, right after the dialog closed — before the wizard had even opened, let alone before a printer existed to report. Nothing ever told Home to check again once the real work finished.

The fix ([ShellController.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.hpp), [ShellController.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp), [PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterSetupLauncher.cpp)): added a small `refresh_home()` method on the shell controller, and call it right after the wizard finishes naming the new printer. Now Home updates live, no restart needed.

**Bug 2 — clicking "Printer settings…", "Rename", or "Remove printer…" in a printer's menu did nothing.**

This one turned out to be a real, production-affecting bug, not a testing artifact — I only found it because I dug into the actual DOM event sequence rather than trusting that "the menu closed" meant "something happened." The menu has a `onBlur` handler meant to close it when focus moves elsewhere (e.g., pressing Tab to leave). But WebKit (Safari's engine, which is what JusPrin's embedded browser view uses on macOS) has a long-standing quirk: clicking a `<button>` with the mouse does *not* give it keyboard focus, unlike Chrome or Firefox. So every mouse click on a menu item fired a blur event with no "where focus went" information, and the code read that as "focus left the menu" and closed it — a fraction of a second before the click on that same button could actually register. The menu genuinely never received your click; it just looked like it did because it closed anyway.

The fix ([PrinterMenu.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterMenu.tsx)): only close on blur when the browser actually reports where focus went *and* that's outside the menu. Real "outside clicks" are still handled correctly by the existing pointerdown-based listener, which checks the actual click target rather than focus state, so keyboard Tab-away-to-close still works too.

I confirmed both by hand afterward: renamed a printer, opened its native settings tab, and removed it — all working through the real UI, not just the test harness.
